terms.definition: A layer of space around the nucleus, at a fixed distance, where electrons orbit.
terms.function: Organizes electrons into layers and sets the atom's reactivity via its outer layer.
terms.whereItIs: The two translucent rings around the sodium nucleus.
terms.whyItMatters: Shells are the architecture that decides how atoms bond.

terms.definition: A shell closer to the nucleus, filled before the outer shells.
terms.function: Holds electrons without participating in bonding.
terms.whereItIs: The inner ring with its two electron dots.
terms.whyItMatters: Inner shells are what the outer chemistry sits on top of.

terms.definition: The electrons in the outermost shell of an atom.
terms.function: The electrons that bond — shared, lost, or gained in reactions.
terms.whereItIs: The single bright electron on sodium's outer ring.
terms.whyItMatters: Valence electrons are the entire basis of chemical bonding.

terms.definition: An outermost shell that holds its maximum number of electrons.
terms.function: Makes an atom stable and unreactive — the noble gas state.
terms.whereItIs: Shown by the calm neon icon in the reactivity layer.
terms.whyItMatters: The drive to fill the outer shell is what pushes atoms to react.
